```{r setup}
library(jsonlite)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

# Every number on this page is read from one extract, written by
# tools/locus_leads_prototype_extract.py from the engine's committed prototype
# outputs. Nothing here computes a statistic: the code below picks and formats.
x <- fromJSON("../data/locus-leads-prototype.json", simplifyDataFrame = TRUE)

n <- function(v) formatC(v, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
f <- function(v, d = 3) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
pct <- function(v, d = 1) paste0(formatC(100 * v, format = "f", digits = d), "%")
sec <- function(v, d = 2) paste0(formatC(v, format = "f", digits = d), " s")
times <- function(v, d = 1) paste0(formatC(v, format = "f", digits = d), "×")
g <- function(v) vapply(v, function(e) format(e, scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE, trim = TRUE), "")
w_lab <- function(w) paste(g(w / 1e6), "Mb")
nz <- function(v) if (is.null(v)) NA else v  # a JSON null inside an object reads as NULL
d_lab <- function(d) { d <- nz(d); ifelse(is.na(d), "bp only", paste(g(d), "cM")) }
pt_lab <- function(d, w) { d <- nz(d); ifelse(is.na(d), paste0("bp only, W ", w_lab(w)), paste0("D ", g(d), " cM, W ", w_lab(w))) }
sci <- function(v) {
  e <- floor(log10(v) + 1e-9)
  paste0(g(signif(v / 10^e, 3)), "×10^−", -e, "^")
}
yes <- function(v) ifelse(v, "yes", "no")
# A count as a word, for counts that read as words in a sentence; numerals past nine.
word <- function(k) if (k <= 9) c("no", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine")[k + 1] else n(k)
Word <- function(k) { w <- word(k); paste0(toupper(substr(w, 1, 1)), substr(w, 2, nchar(w))) }
w_list <- function(ws) { ws <- unlist(ws); if (length(ws) == 0) "no W" else paste("W", paste(w_lab(ws), collapse = ", ")) }
# The share of an Analysis's top-tier rows #406 counted past |z| 38, matched by Analysis.
over_share <- function(ids) vapply(ids, function(id) x$cost$slices$share_abs_z_over[
  x$cost$slices$analysis_id == id & x$cost$slices$threshold == x$method$grid$tier], 0)
pick <- function(df, d, w) { d <- nz(d); df[(if (is.na(d)) is.na(df$d_cm) else (!is.na(df$d_cm) & df$d_cm == d)) & df$w_bp == w, ] }

M <- x$method
GRID <- M$grid
R2P <- g(GRID$r2[1])
R2L <- g(GRID$r2[2])
TIER <- sci(GRID$tier)
CC <- M$count_criteria
PL <- M$per_lead_criteria
TR <- x$tracer
EUR <- x$eur
EC <- EUR$counts
EPL <- EUR$per_lead
AN <- x$ancestries
MP <- x$maps
CO <- x$cost
PR <- x$profile
PV <- CO$per_variant_cm
NAMED_W <- EC$named$w_bp
NAMED <- pt_lab(EC$named$d_cm, NAMED_W)
NEAR <- pt_lab(EPL$nearest$d_cm, EPL$nearest$w_bp)
TP_D <- TR$d_cm
TP_W <- TR$w_bp
TP <- pt_lab(TP_D, TP_W)
# Where #409's rules meet C3: at #403's named W, and anywhere else.
C3A <- PR$c3_anywhere
C3_AT_NAMED <- if (length(C3A) == 0) character(0) else C3A$label[C3A$w_bp == NAMED_W]
C3_ALL <- if (length(C3A) == 0) character(0) else paste0(C3A$label, " at W ", w_lab(C3A$w_bp))
C3_OTHER <- if (length(C3A) == 0) C3A else C3A[C3A$w_bp != NAMED_W, ]
C3_ELSEWHERE <- if (length(C3_OTHER) == 0 || nrow(C3_OTHER) == 0) "no rule meets C3 either" else
  paste(paste0(C3_OTHER$label, " meets C3 at W ", w_lab(C3_OTHER$w_bp), " (Δρ ", sprintf("%+.3f", C3_OTHER$delta_rho),
               ", density gain ", sprintf("%+.3f", C3_OTHER$delta_abs_log2), " in median |log2|)"), collapse = "; ")
OKABE <- c("#0072B2", "#E69F00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "#56B4E9", "#D55E00")
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom"))

# Figure captions computed from the extract (YAML cannot hold the R inline).
CAP_TRADEOFF <- paste0("Spurious splits against lost signals, pooled over the ", EUR$swept, " swept EUR Analyses at r² ", R2P, ". Each line is one W; its circles are the D values, left to right from the smallest (labelled on the W ", w_lab(NAMED_W), " line), and its open square is the bp-only rule. The shaded corner is where both rates meet the per-lead criteria, and no point reaches it: a smaller D buys fewer lost signals at the price of more spurious splits.")
CAP_BY_PEAK <- paste0("Lost signals per Analysis at ", TP, " against the Analysis's largest |z| (log scale), r² ", R2P, ". Analyses with strong peaks lose far more of plink2's index variants, because r² ", R2P, " clumping keeps the shoulders of a strong peak as separate index variants. The labelled Analysis is the one discussed in the text.")
CAP_COUNTS <- paste0("The count criteria at every (D, W) for the ", EC$analyses, " EUR Analyses. C1 holds above the horizontal line (Spearman ρ ≥ ", g(CC$rho_min), "); the shaded band is C2's range for the median density ratio (C2's second leg, on the median |log2|, is in the table below). Open squares are bp-only. Every point clears C1; only D ", paste(g(unlist(EC$c2_fails_at_d)), collapse = ", "), " cM falls out of the band, and bp-only at W ", w_lab(NAMED_W), " comes closest to finding as many loci on HapMap3 as on the full shared set.")
CAP_CURVES <- paste0("ρ (C1, top) and the median density ratio (C2, bottom) against D for each ancestry, at W ", w_lab(GRID$w_bp[2]), " and W ", w_lab(NAMED_W), "; the right-most point is bp-only. Above the line is C1; inside the band is C2's ratio range. EUR and EAS stay high on ρ and reach the band; AFR's ρ collapses as D grows; AMR keeps its ρ but never reaches the band.")
```

## Question and result

`n_hits_*`, the Top-Hit Counts in a Store's `analyses.tsv`, count an Analysis's
associations past each significance threshold. They mix two things: how many
loci an Analysis has, and how densely its variant axis is typed. A
Reference-Completed Store and a HapMap3-density Store give the same locus very
different hit counts. opengwas/opengwasdb#62 proposed a second count beside them,
`n_loci_*`, that counts **Locus Leads**: one lead per locus, chosen by a pruning
rule that uses genetic distance in centimorgans (cM) as a stand-in for linkage
disequilibrium (LD) clumping, so that neither a build nor a query needs an LD
reference panel. This report gathers what the
prototype tickets found when they held that rule against real plink2 clumping.

**Result.** For European (EUR) Analyses, a count of Locus Leads ranks Analyses
as the count of clumps does, and it is far less sensitive to variant density
than a count of hits. But for EUR and East Asian (EAS) Analyses a plain
base-pair (bp) window does as well as any genetic-distance rule, and no rule
agrees with clumping lead by lead. The
owner has therefore decided that `n_loci_*` uses a bp-only window of
`r w_lab(NAMED_W)` (megabases, millions of bp) for EUR and EAS, with no cM condition and no per-variant cM
array, and that African (AFR) and admixed American (AMR) Analyses get no
`n_loci_*` until they are calibrated. Whether pruning also runs per query is
still open.

The prototype's code is throwaway; it lives in the engine's
`prototypes/locus_leads/` on the integration branch `orch/62-locus-leads`. Its
outputs were committed under `docs/benchmark-output/locus_leads/`, and every
number below is read from them at engine commit
`r substr(x$engine$commit, 1, 7)` (see [Reproduce](#reproduce)).

## The question

### The proposal

[The proposal on #62](https://github.com/opengwas/opengwasdb/issues/62) adds
`n_loci_5e8`, `n_loci_5e6` and `n_loci_5e4` beside the `n_hits_*` columns, and a
Locus Lead option for the Top-Hit Query. A Locus Lead is not an *independent*
signal: neither this rule nor clumping is conditional analysis. The rule ranks
on |z|, never on p. A float64 two-sided p is 0 from |z| ≈
`r f(M$p_zero_abs_z, 1)`, and the strongest Analyses in our Stores go well past
that, so ranking on p would tie the strongest variants of a big locus.

### The ancestry-specific revision

[The revision](https://github.com/opengwas/opengwasdb/issues/62) replaced the
single pedigree map of the first proposal with **ancestry-specific maps**, one
per Store. LD decays faster per cM where effective population size is larger,
as in AFR, so one cM leaves less LD there than in EUR. The revision therefore
calibrates D per ancestry, each on its own genotype panel, and predicts two
things the prototype tested: that AFR needs a smaller D than EUR, and that the
AMR map, built from admixed samples, is the least trustworthy.

### What the prototype tickets asked

| ticket | question |
|---|---|
| [#402](https://github.com/opengwas/opengwasdb/issues/402) | Does the comparison work end to end on one EUR Analysis? |
| [#403](https://github.com/opengwas/opengwasdb/issues/403) | Across EUR Analyses, is there a D and W that matches clumping, and does cM beat a plain bp window? |
| [#404](https://github.com/opengwas/opengwasdb/issues/404) | Is the published pyrho EUR map good enough, or does another map do better? |
| [#405](https://github.com/opengwas/opengwasdb/issues/405) | Does the method work for AFR, EAS and AMR, and with what D? |
| [#406](https://github.com/opengwas/opengwasdb/issues/406) | Is pruning cheaper than clumping, and fast enough to run per query? |
| [#409](https://github.com/opengwas/opengwasdb/issues/409) | Do locus boundaries taken from the data (peak prominence, LD blocks) beat a fixed distance? |

: The prototype tickets, each a sub-issue of #62.

## Method

### The Locus Lead rule

For each Analysis, tier and chromosome, take the tier's rows in descending |z|,
with ties broken by ascending Variant Index (a row's place in the Store Variant
Table). Accept a row as a Locus Lead unless an already-accepted lead lies within
**W bp and D cM** of it. D does the main work: it splits signals across a
recombination hotspot, which a bp window would merge. W caps merging where cM
barely moves over megabases, such as centromeres and inversions. With D set to
infinity the rule becomes a plain bp window of width W, the **bp-only** rule,
which every sweep runs as its baseline.

```{r rule-diagram}
#| fig-cap: "The rule on a toy chromosome. A is the strongest hit and becomes a Locus Lead. B lies within W bp and within D cM of A, so it merges into A. C lies within W bp of A, but a recombination hotspot puts it more than D cM away, so it becomes a lead. E lies within D cM of C, where cM barely moves, but more than W bp from it, so it becomes a lead too. The shaded spans are A's D window (top) and A's W window (bottom)."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
pos <- seq(0, 100, by = 0.5)
cm_at <- function(p) ifelse(p < 50, 0.02 * p, ifelse(p < 52, 1 + (p - 50) * 0.75, ifelse(p < 75, 2.5 + (p - 52) * 0.02, 2.96)))
hits <- data.frame(id = c("A", "B", "C", "E"), pos = c(30, 40, 60, 97), z = c(12, 8, 9, 6),
                   outcome = c("Locus Lead", "merged into A", "Locus Lead", "Locus Lead"))
panel_levels <- c("genetic map (cM)", "|z| of the tier's rows")
map_df <- data.frame(pos = pos, value = cm_at(pos), panel = factor(panel_levels[1], panel_levels))
hit_df <- transform(hits, panel = factor(panel_levels[2], panel_levels))
mark_df <- transform(hits, value = cm_at(pos), panel = factor(panel_levels[1], panel_levels))
d_band <- data.frame(panel = factor(panel_levels[1], panel_levels), ymin = cm_at(30) - 0.5, ymax = cm_at(30) + 0.5)
w_band <- data.frame(panel = factor(panel_levels[2], panel_levels), xmin = 30 - 35, xmax = 30 + 35)
ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = d_band, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), fill = "grey85") +
  geom_rect(data = w_band, aes(xmin = pmax(xmin, 0), xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf), fill = "grey85") +
  geom_line(data = map_df, aes(pos, value), colour = "grey30") +
  geom_point(data = mark_df, aes(pos, value), colour = "grey30", size = 1.5) +
  geom_text(data = mark_df, aes(pos, value, label = id), nudge_x = -2.5, nudge_y = 0.25, size = 3.5) +
  geom_segment(data = hit_df, aes(x = pos, xend = pos, y = 0, yend = z, colour = outcome), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = hit_df, aes(pos, z, colour = outcome), size = 2.5) +
  geom_text(data = hit_df, aes(pos, z, label = id), nudge_y = 1.3, size = 3.5) +
  geom_text(data = data.frame(panel = factor(panel_levels[1], panel_levels), pos = 51, value = cm_at(52)),
            aes(pos, value, label = "hotspot"), hjust = 1.15, vjust = -0.6, size = 3, colour = "grey30") +
  facet_grid(panel ~ ., scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Locus Lead" = OKABE[1], "merged into A" = OKABE[2]), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "position on the chromosome (bp)", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), strip.placement = "outside", panel.grid = element_blank())
```

### Genetic maps

The maps are the published pyrho maps (Spence and Song, *Science Advances*):
recombination maps inferred from LD in each 1000 Genomes population, so they
reflect historical recombination. They were released on Zenodo
(<`r M$map$record`>, archive md5 `` `r M$map$md5` ``, checked on every load).
Each ancestry's map is the equal-weight mean of its populations' maps. cM is
interpolated linearly between map points, held flat beyond a chromosome's ends,
and left missing on a chromosome the map does not cover (X, Y and MT), never
replaced by a substitute value.

```{r map-populations}
pops <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(AN), function(a) {
  p <- unlist(AN[[a]]$populations)
  data.frame(ancestry = a, populations = paste(names(p), collapse = ", "),
             maps = length(p), weight = f(unique(round(p, 12)), 3))
}))
kable(pops, col.names = c("ancestry", "1000 Genomes populations", "maps averaged", "weight of each"),
      caption = "The populations averaged into each ancestry's map, with the weights each map records.")
```

The EUR mean carries `r word(EUR$spike_count)` jumps that come from one population's map each. #402
found them, and #403 measured them from the population maps:

```{r spikes}
sp <- EUR$spikes
kable(data.frame(population = sp$population, position = paste0("chr", sp$chromosome, ":", n(sp$position)),
                 interval = paste(n(sp$interval_bp), "bp"), pop = paste(f(sp$population_cm, 2), "cM"),
                 mean = paste(f(sp$mean_map_cm, 2), "cM")),
      col.names = c("population", "map point", "interval to the next point", "the population's map gains",
                    "the EUR mean keeps"),
      caption = paste0("The ", word(EUR$spike_count), " single-population spikes in the pyrho EUR mean. Hits on either side of one never merge under a cM rule."))
```

### The reference: plink2 clumping

Clumping runs `plink2 --clump` on the HGDP+1kGP genotype panels (the Human
Genome Diversity Project and 1000 Genomes samples, as gnomAD released them),
split by super-population, each Analysis against its own ancestry's panel:
index p `r sci(M$clump$p1)`, a window of `r n(M$clump$kb)` kb (kilobases,
thousands of bp), and r²
computed `r M$clump$r2_mode` because the panels carry no phase. plink2 is
given −log10 p computed from z, with equal values separated in the rule's
order, so both methods rank rows identically even where p underflows.

The primary threshold is **r² `r R2P`**; r² `r R2L`, the old OpenGWAS default,
is reported beside it. The panels are small (EUR `r n(AN$EUR$samples)`, AFR
`r n(AN$AFR$samples)`, EAS `r n(AN$EAS$samples)` and AMR `r n(AN$AMR$samples)`
samples), and at these sizes unlinked variants reach a low r² by chance. Among
variant pairs on different chromosomes in the EUR panel,
`r pct(AN$EUR$chance_panel[["share_r2_ge_0.001"]])` reach r² `r R2L` and
`r pct(AN$EUR$chance_panel[["share_r2_ge_0.01"]], 2)` reach r² `r R2P`. So r²
`r R2L` mostly measures noise at this sample size, and r² `r R2P` is the
reference every criterion is judged against.

### The shared set

Both methods see the same rows. Each sweep reads an Analysis's Observed
Associations at the `r TIER` tier, the rows a Top-Hit Query returns at
p ≤ `r TIER` (Imputed Associations are left out), and keeps
the rows matched to the panel by chromosome, position and allele set that also
have a finite cM. Every other row is counted under exactly one reason (off the
panel's chromosomes, absent at its position, other alleles, ambiguous, or no
cM), so none is dropped silently. An Analysis with less than
`r pct(EUR$below_floor$floor, 0)` of its rows in the shared set is recorded and
not swept.

### Two ways to judge a rule

**Per lead.** A *spurious split* is `r M$definitions$spurious_split`; a *lost
signal* is `r M$definitions$lost_signal`. The rates are
`r M$definitions$spurious_split_rate` and `r M$definitions$lost_signal_rate`.
#403 fixed its working criteria before it ran: at r² `r PL$at_r2`, spurious
splits at most `r pct(PL$spurious_split_rate_max, 0)` of Locus Leads **and**
lost signals at most `r pct(PL$lost_signal_rate_max, 0)` of index variants, and
clearly better than bp-only at the same W (a pooled disagreement rate at most
`r pct(PL$clearly_better_pooled_at_most, 0)` of bp-only's, and lower in at least
`r pct(PL$clearly_better_analyses_lower_at_least, 0)` of the Analyses where the
two differ).

**Per Analysis, by counts.** `n_loci_*` is one number per Analysis, so after
#403 the owner decided to judge rules by counts, with the per-lead rates kept as
diagnostics. The count criteria were written into #403's output before they
were computed, in this wording:

- **C1:** `r CC$C1`
- **C2:** `r CC$C2`
- **C3:** `r CC$C3`
- Reading of C3: `r CC$c3_reading`
- The point named: `r CC$named`

HapMap3 (HM3 in the criteria) here is the list of `r n(M$hm3$alids)` HapMap3
variants on GRCh38 (the Genome Reference Consortium's human build 38, the
assembly every Store, map and panel here uses), standing in for a sparse variant axis such as a
HapMap3-density Store's. A rule that is insensitive to variant
density finds about as many loci on it as on the full shared set.

## Results by ticket

### #402: the tracer on one EUR Analysis

**Question.** Does a comparison of Locus Leads with plink2 clumping run end to
end on one well-powered Analysis, with every row accounted for?

**Criteria.** The map archive's checksum is checked before use; interpolated cM
never decreases along a chromosome; off-panel rows and rows with no cM are
counted, not dropped; both methods choose the same lead among ties at p = 0; a
synthetic fixture splits across a hotspot and merges in a cold region; and the
output reproduces. The engine's tests check the checksum, the monotone map, the
tie order and the hotspot; the committed output records every count and both
rates, a re-run reproduced it byte for byte, and its row categories add up to
the tier, which the extract for this page checks.
**Met.**

**Result.** `r TR$analysis_id` (`r TR$analysis_label`) in `r TR$store` has
`r n(TR$tier_rows)` Observed Associations at `r TIER` and
`r n(TR$imputed)` imputed. `r pct(TR$shared_set_share)` of them are in the
shared set. `r n(TR$ties$tied_rows)` rows sit in `r n(TR$ties$tied_groups)` runs
of tied |z|, which is why the tie order matters even below the p = 0 range.

```{r tracer-partition}
pt <- unlist(TR$partition)
labels <- c(shared_set = "shared set", matched_no_cm = "on the panel, no cM",
            off_panel_chromosome = "off the panel's chromosomes", absent_at_position = "absent at its position",
            allele_mismatch = "other alleles", ambiguous = "ambiguous")
kable(data.frame(category = labels[names(pt)], rows = n(pt)), row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("category", "rows"),
      caption = paste0("Where each of ", TR$analysis_id, "'s ", n(TR$tier_rows), " tier rows went. The categories add up to the tier."))
```

```{r tracer-rates}
br <- TR$by_r2
kable(data.frame(r2 = names(br),
                 leads = n(sapply(br, `[[`, "locus_leads")), index = n(sapply(br, `[[`, "index_variants")),
                 agreed = n(sapply(br, `[[`, "agreed")),
                 split = paste0(n(sapply(br, `[[`, "spurious_splits")), " (", pct(sapply(br, `[[`, "spurious_split_rate")), ")"),
                 lost = paste0(n(sapply(br, `[[`, "lost_signals")), " (", pct(sapply(br, `[[`, "lost_signal_rate")), ")")),
      row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("clumping r²", "Locus Leads", "index variants", "agreed", "spurious splits (rate)", "lost signals (rate)"),
      caption = paste0("Locus Leads at ", TP, " against plink2's index variants, for ", TR$analysis_id, "."))
```

At r² `r R2P`, `r n(TR$splits_beyond_w)` of the
`r n(TR$by_r2[[R2P]]$spurious_splits)` spurious splits lie further than W from
the stronger index variant whose clump holds them (the median distance over all
of them is `r f(TR$splits_median_distance_bp / 1e6, 2)` Mb). That pointed at chance r²
at this panel size, which #403 then measured. The tracer also found the
`r word(EUR$spike_count)` map spikes above.

### #403: the EUR sweep

**Question.** Across many EUR Analyses, is there a (D, W) at which Locus Leads
match plink2's r² `r R2P` clumping, and does the cM condition do better than a
plain bp window of the same W?

**The Analyses.** `r n(EUR$selection$drawn)` Analyses were drawn with seed
`r EUR$selection$seed` from `r n(EUR$selection$pool)` EUR Analyses (by Assigned
Ancestry) in the genome-wide Stores, stratified by observed `r TIER` rows and by
largest |z|, with at least `r EUR$selection$quota_z` of largest |z| ≥
`r EUR$selection$quota_z_from` and `r EUR$selection$quota_p_zero` past the p = 0
point.
`r n(EUR$selection$no_observed_rows)` pool Analyses had no Observed Association
at the tier and could not be drawn. Analyses with more than
`r n(EUR$selection$max_observed_rows)` observed rows were left out of the pool:
`r paste(EUR$selection$excluded_over_max_rows$analysis_id, collapse = " and ")`, whose
largest |z| are `r paste(f(EUR$selection$excluded_over_max_rows$max_abs_z, 1), collapse = " and ")`
([#406](#cost) found
`r paste(pct(over_share(EUR$selection$excluded_over_max_rows$analysis_id), 0), collapse = " and ")`
of their tier rows past |z| `r CO$slices$over_abs_z[1]`, where p is close to
underflowing, which looks like an artefact of their sources).
`r n(length(EUR$below_floor$analyses$analysis_id))`
drawn Analyses fell under the shared-set floor
(`r paste0(EUR$below_floor$analyses$analysis_id, " ", pct(EUR$below_floor$analyses$shared_set_share), collapse = ", ")`),
so `r n(EUR$swept)` were swept: `r n(EUR$swept_strong)`
with largest |z| ≥ `r EUR$selection$quota_z_from`. They hold `r n(EUR$rows$tier)` Observed Associations at the
tier, `r pct(EUR$rows$shared_share)` of them in the shared set. The grid is
D ∈ {`r paste(g(GRID$d_cm), collapse = ", ")`} cM ×
W ∈ {`r paste(g(GRID$w_bp / 1e6), collapse = ", ")`} Mb, plus bp-only at each W.

#### The per-lead judgement: not met

**No (D, W) meets the per-lead criteria.** `r n(EPL$qualifying)` of the
`r n(nrow(EPL$points))` points qualify. The nearest, by the larger of its two
rates, is `r NEAR`: `r pct(EPL$nearest$spurious_split_rate)` spurious splits and
`r pct(EPL$nearest$lost_signal_rate)` lost signals. The plain
`r w_lab(EPL$nearest$w_bp)` window gives
`r pct(EPL$nearest_bp_only$spurious_split_rate)` and `r pct(EPL$nearest_bp_only$lost_signal_rate)`. Lost signals never fall below
`r pct(EPL$lost_rate_min)` anywhere on the grid. Spurious splits reach the
`r pct(PL$spurious_split_rate_max, 0)` limit only at
`r n(EPL$low_spurious_points)` points, all with W of at least
`r w_lab(EPL$low_spurious_w_min)`, and there lost signals are at least `r pct(EPL$low_spurious_lost_min)`. A cM condition trades lost signals for
spurious splits; it never gets both down.

```{r eur-tradeoff}
#| fig-cap: !expr CAP_TRADEOFF
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.8
pts <- EPL$points
pts$W <- factor(w_lab(pts$w_bp), levels = w_lab(GRID$w_bp))
cmp <- pts[!is.na(pts$d_cm), ]
cmp <- cmp[order(cmp$w_bp, cmp$d_cm), ]
bpo <- pts[is.na(pts$d_cm), ]
ggplot() +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = PL$lost_signal_rate_max, ymin = 0, ymax = PL$spurious_split_rate_max, fill = "grey85") +
  geom_path(data = cmp, aes(lost_signal_rate, spurious_split_rate, colour = W, group = W)) +
  geom_point(data = cmp, aes(lost_signal_rate, spurious_split_rate, colour = W), size = 2) +
  geom_text(data = cmp[cmp$w_bp == NAMED_W, ], aes(lost_signal_rate, spurious_split_rate, colour = W, label = paste(g(d_cm), "cM")),
            nudge_x = 0.035, nudge_y = 0.004, size = 2.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = bpo, aes(lost_signal_rate, spurious_split_rate, colour = W), shape = 0, size = 3.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = OKABE) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(v) pct(v, 0), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(v) pct(v, 0), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = "lost signals / index variants", y = "spurious splits / Locus Leads", colour = "W")
```

Two things made per-lead agreement the wrong yardstick for a count:

- **r² `r R2P` clumping splits strong peaks into their LD shadows.** A variant
  with r² `r R2P` to a lead of |z| z is expected at |z| ≈ z·√r², still far past
  the `r TIER` line (|z| `r f(M$z_at_tier, 2)`) when z is large. Lost signals
  therefore rise with peak strength: at `r TP`, they run
  `r pct(EPL$by_peak$weak_min, 0)`–`r pct(EPL$by_peak$weak_max, 0)` for the
  `r EPL$by_peak$weak_n` Analyses with largest |z| below
  `r g(EPL$by_peak$weak_below)`, and
  `r pct(EPL$by_peak$strong_min, 0)`–`r pct(EPL$by_peak$strong_max, 0)` for the
  `r EPL$by_peak$strong_n` at or above `r g(EPL$by_peak$strong_from)`.
  `r EPL$named_analysis$analysis_id` (largest |z| `r f(EPL$named_analysis$max_abs_z, 0)`) has
  `r EPL$named_analysis$locus_leads` Locus Leads against
  `r EPL$named_analysis$index_variants` clumps: at that strength a variant with
  r² `r R2L` to the lead is still expected at |z| ≈
  `r f(EPL$named_analysis[["expected_z_at_legacy_r2"]], 1)`, past `r TIER`.
- **r² `r R2L` is mostly noise at n = `r n(AN$EUR$samples)`.** Across the swept
  Analyses' index variants, `r pct(EPL$chance_index_pairs[["share_r2_ge_0.001"]], 0)`
  of cross-chromosome pairs exceed r² `r R2L`, and
  `r pct(EPL$chance_index_pairs[["share_r2_ge_0.01"]], 2)` exceed r² `r R2P`
  (`r n(EPL$chance_index_pairs$pairs_evaluable)` pairs). At `r NEAR`,
  `r n(EPL$nearest_splits$beyond_1mb)` of the `r n(EPL$nearest_splits$n)`
  spurious splits are more than `r w_lab(EPL$nearest_splits$near_band_bp)`
  from the variant whose clump holds them.

```{r eur-by-peak}
#| fig-cap: !expr CAP_BY_PEAK
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.2
pa <- EUR$per_analysis
pa$label <- ifelse(pa$analysis_id == EPL$named_analysis$analysis_id, pa$analysis_id, "")
ggplot(pa, aes(max_abs_z, lost_rate_tracer_point)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = index_variants), colour = OKABE[1], alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), nudge_y = 0.05, size = 3) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(v) pct(v, 0), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_size_area(name = "index variants", max_size = 6) +
  labs(x = "largest |z| in the Analysis", y = "lost signals / index variants")
```

The spikes matter little: at `r NEAR`,
`r n(EPL$nearest_spikes$straddling[EPL$nearest_spikes$kind == "spurious_split_pairs"])`
of `r n(EPL$nearest_spikes$n[EPL$nearest_spikes$kind == "spurious_split_pairs"])`
spurious splits and
`r n(EPL$nearest_spikes$straddling[EPL$nearest_spikes$kind == "lost_signal_pairs"])`
of `r n(EPL$nearest_spikes$n[EPL$nearest_spikes$kind == "lost_signal_pairs"])`
lost signals span either spike.

#### The count judgement: C1 and C2 met, C3 not

```{r eur-counts}
#| fig-cap: !expr CAP_COUNTS
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.6
cf <- EC$configs
cf$W <- factor(w_lab(cf$w_bp), levels = w_lab(GRID$w_bp))
ccm <- cf[!is.na(cf$d_cm), ]
ccm <- ccm[order(ccm$w_bp, ccm$d_cm), ]
cbp <- cf[is.na(cf$d_cm), ]
ggplot() +
  annotate("rect", xmin = CC$ratio_range[1], xmax = CC$ratio_range[2], ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey88") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = CC$rho_min, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_path(data = ccm, aes(median_ratio, rho, colour = W, group = W)) +
  geom_point(data = ccm, aes(median_ratio, rho, colour = W), size = 2) +
  geom_point(data = cbp, aes(median_ratio, rho, colour = W), shape = 0, size = 3.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = OKABE) +
  labs(x = "median density ratio, leads on HapMap3 / leads on the shared set", y = "Spearman ρ, Locus Leads vs index variants", colour = "W")
```

- **C1 holds at `r EC$c1_met` of `r EC$points` points**, with ρ from
  `r f(EC$rho_min)` to `r f(EC$rho_max)`. Counting Locus Leads ranks Analyses
  as clumping does.
- **C2 holds at `r EC$c2_met` of `r EC$points` points**; it fails only at D
  `r paste(g(unlist(EC$c2_fails_at_d)), collapse = ", ")` cM. Raw rows keep a
  median of `r f(EC$rows$median_ratio)` of their count on HapMap3 (median |log2| `r f(EC$rows$median_abs_log2)`), so C2 asks the leads' median |log2| to be at
  most `r f(EC$rows$c2_abs_log2_limit)`. Leads are far less density-sensitive
  than rows.
- **The point named is `r NAMED`**, which loses
  `r pct(EC$named$lost_to_density)` of its leads when only HapMap3 variants are
  present. The best cM point is `r pt_lab(EC$named_cm$d_cm, EC$named_cm$w_bp)`,
  which loses `r pct(EC$named_cm$lost_to_density)`.
- **C3 holds at `r w_list(EC$c3_holds_at_w)`**. The largest gain in ρ any cM
  point makes over bp-only at its W is
  `r sprintf("%+.4f", EC$largest_rho_gain$delta_rho)`
  (`r pt_lab(EC$largest_rho_gain$d_cm, EC$largest_rho_gain$w_bp)`), against a
  margin of `r g(CC$c3_margin_rho)`, and it costs
  `r f(-EC$largest_rho_gain$delta_abs_log2)` in median |log2|, against a margin
  of `r g(CC$c3_margin_abs_log2)`. The best |log2| gain any cM point makes is `r f(EC$best_abs_log2_gain)`. In EUR, cM adds nothing the counts can see.

```{r eur-c3}
c3 <- EC$c3
kable(data.frame(W = w_lab(c3$w_bp), rho = f(c3$bp_only_rho), log2 = f(c3$bp_only_median_abs_log2),
                 best = d_lab(c3$largest_rho_gain$d_cm), dr = sprintf("%+.4f", c3$largest_rho_gain$delta_rho),
                 dl = sprintf("%+.3f", c3$largest_rho_gain$delta_abs_log2), holds = yes(c3$holds)),
      col.names = c("W", "bp-only ρ", "bp-only median |log2|", "cM point with the largest ρ gain", "Δρ", "Δ|log2| (positive is better)", "C3 holds"),
      caption = "C3 at each W: the cM point that gains most in ρ over bp-only, and what it does to density sensitivity.")
```

### #404: other maps

**Question.** Is the published pyrho EUR map good enough, or would another map
make a cM condition worth having? The same Analyses, shared set and grid were
run with the **median** of the `r length(AN$EUR$populations)` EUR population
maps (taken over rates per interval, which removes single-population spikes) and with **HapMap II**,
lifted to GRCh38 as Eagle ships it.

**Criteria.** Each map's best (D, W) and per-lead rates beside the pyrho mean's,
on the same rows; a statement of whether the pyrho map is adequate; checksums
verified and cM non-decreasing for each map; the deCODE licence recorded.
**Met**, with deCODE left out.

**deCODE.** The pedigree map from deCODE (Halldorsson et al., *Science*) was
the first proposal's default. Its file and its terms of use could not be
reached from the build node (the publisher's site answers with a bot
challenge), and no open copy or licence was found, so the run left it out
rather than guess at its terms. A pedigree map therefore remains untested.

**Result.** Every map leaves exactly the same shared set:
`r n(MP$shared_set$rows)` of `r n(MP$shared_set$tier_rows)` tier rows
(`r pct(MP$shared_set$share)`), with one digest over all
`r MP$shared_set$analyses_checked` drawn Analyses.
`r if (MP$c3_nowhere) "None of the maps makes C3 hold at any W:" else "C3 holds for some map at some W:"`

```{r maps}
mp <- MP$maps
spike_txt <- function(s) paste(paste0("chr", s$chromosome, " ", f(s$cm_gain, 3)), collapse = "; ")
kable(data.frame(map = mp$name, length = paste(f(mp$total_cm, 1), "cM"),
                 c1 = paste(mp$c1_met, "of", mp$points_judged), c2 = paste(mp$c2_met, "of", mp$points_judged),
                 c3 = vapply(mp$c3_holds_at_w, w_list, ""),
                 named = pt_lab(mp$named$d_cm, mp$named$w_bp), lost = pct(mp$named$lost_to_density),
                 best = paste0(pt_lab(mp$named_cm$d_cm, mp$named_cm$w_bp), " (", pct(mp$named_cm$lost_to_density), ")"),
                 drho = sprintf("%+.4f", mp$largest_rho_gain),
                 per_lead = paste0(pt_lab(mp$best_per_lead$d_cm, mp$best_per_lead$w_bp),
                                   ifelse(mp$best_per_lead$qualifies, "", " (none qualifies)"), ": ",
                                   pct(mp$best_per_lead$spurious_split_rate), " / ", pct(mp$best_per_lead$lost_signal_rate)),
                 rates = paste0(pct(mp$tracer_point$spurious_split_rate), " / ", pct(mp$tracer_point$lost_signal_rate)),
                 spikes = vapply(mp$spike_gain_cm, spike_txt, ""),
                 clamped = n(mp$clamped$rows)),
      col.names = c("map", "genetic length", "C1 held at", "C2 held at", "C3 holds at", "point named", "its leads lost to density",
                    "best cM point (lost to density)", "largest Δρ over bp-only",
                    "best per-lead point: spurious / lost", paste0("spurious / lost at ", TP),
                    "cM gained across the spike intervals", "shared-set rows clamped at a map end"),
      caption = paste0("The EUR maps on #403's Analyses, shared set and grid. The best per-lead point is #403's: the qualifying (D, W) with the lowest disagreement or, when none qualifies, the one whose larger rate is smallest. Per-lead rates are at r² ", R2P, "; the spike column is the cM each map puts across the intervals where the pyrho mean jumps."))
```

- **The pyrho EUR map is adequate, and the map is not the lever.**
  `r if (MP$same_named_point) paste0("Every map names the same point, ", pt_lab(mp$named$d_cm[1], mp$named$w_bp[1]), ", where cM is not read at all.") else "The maps name different points."`
- **The median removes both spikes** without changing the verdict.
- **HapMap II is `r pct(MP$hapmap2_length_over_mean - 1, 0)` longer** in cM than
  the pyrho mean, so a given D covers fewer bp; it turns lost signals into
  spurious splits. `r if (MP$largest_rho_gain_map == "hapmap2") "Its largest ρ gain over bp-only is the biggest of the maps, and it still fails C3's density margin." else ""`
- Rows outside a map's first or last point take that point's cM, held flat:
  HapMap II clamps `r n(mp$clamped$rows[mp$name == "hapmap2"])` shared-set rows
  this way (`r n(mp$clamped$before_first_knot[mp$name == "hapmap2"])` before its
  first point, `r n(mp$clamped$after_last_knot[mp$name == "hapmap2"])` after its
  last), the pyrho mean `r n(mp$clamped$rows[mp$name == "pyrho-mean"])`.
  Neither comparison map lost a point to the non-decreasing check
  (`r paste(n(mp$points_dropped[!is.na(mp$points_dropped)]), collapse = " and ")` points dropped).

### #405: AFR, EAS and AMR

**Question.** Does the method work beyond EUR, and with what D per ancestry? It
also tests the revision's two predictions: AFR needs a smaller D than EUR, and
the AMR map is the least trustworthy.

**Criteria.** For each ancestry: a seeded, recorded draw; the best (D, W) or why
none qualifies; per-lead rates at both r²; D compared with EUR's; the
population weights recorded; whether the AMR map is usable. The same grid, count
criteria and row cap as #403, each ancestry against its own map and panel, with
seed `r AN$AFR$seed`.

```{r ancestries}
an <- names(AN)
row_of <- function(a) {
  r <- AN[[a]]
  c <- r$counts
  named <- if (is.null(c$named)) "none" else pt_lab(c$named$d_cm, c$named$w_bp)
  c3w <- if (length(c$c3_holds_at_w) == 0) "no W" else paste(w_lab(unlist(c$c3_holds_at_w)), collapse = ", ")
  data.frame(ancestry = a, stores = paste(r$stores, collapse = ", "),
             draw = paste0(n(r$pool), " / ", n(r$drawn), " / ", n(r$swept)),
             below = n(r$below_floor), rows = n(r$tier_rows), shared = pct(r$shared_share),
             c1 = paste(c$c1_met, "of", c$points), c2 = paste(c$c2_met, "of", c$points),
             both = paste(c$both_met, "of", c$points), named = named, c3 = c3w,
             nearest = pt_lab(r$nearest$d_cm, r$nearest$w_bp),
             rates = paste0(pct(r$nearest$primary$spurious_split_rate), " / ", pct(r$nearest$primary$lost_signal_rate)),
             legacy = paste0(pct(r$nearest$legacy$spurious_split_rate), " / ", pct(r$nearest$legacy$lost_signal_rate)))
}
kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(an, row_of)), row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("ancestry", "Store", "pool / drawn / swept", "below the shared-set floor", "tier rows swept",
                    "in the shared set", "C1 held at", "C2 held at", "C1 and C2", "point named", "C3 holds at",
                    "nearest per-lead point", paste0("spurious / lost there, r² ", R2P),
                    paste0("spurious / lost there, r² ", R2L)),
      caption = "Each ancestry's sweep against its own map and panel. EUR's column is #403's.")
```

```{r ancestry-curves}
#| fig-cap: !expr CAP_CURVES
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
d_levels <- c(g(GRID$d_cm), "bp only")
curves <- do.call(rbind, lapply(an, function(a) {
  cf <- AN[[a]]$counts$configs
  cf <- cf[cf$w_bp %in% c(GRID$w_bp[2], NAMED_W), ]
  rbind(data.frame(ancestry = a, W = w_lab(cf$w_bp), D = ifelse(is.na(cf$d_cm), "bp only", g(cf$d_cm)),
                   metric = "Spearman ρ", value = cf$rho),
        data.frame(ancestry = a, W = w_lab(cf$w_bp), D = ifelse(is.na(cf$d_cm), "bp only", g(cf$d_cm)),
                   metric = "median density ratio", value = cf$median_ratio))
}))
curves$D <- factor(curves$D, levels = d_levels)
curves$W <- factor(paste("W", curves$W), levels = paste("W", w_lab(c(GRID$w_bp[2], NAMED_W))))
curves$metric <- factor(curves$metric, levels = c("Spearman ρ", "median density ratio"))
refs_line <- data.frame(metric = factor("Spearman ρ", levels(curves$metric)), y = CC$rho_min)
refs_band <- data.frame(metric = factor("median density ratio", levels(curves$metric)),
                        ymin = CC$ratio_range[1], ymax = CC$ratio_range[2])
ggplot(curves, aes(D, value, colour = ancestry, group = ancestry)) +
  geom_rect(data = refs_band, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey88") +
  geom_hline(data = refs_line, aes(yintercept = y), colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  facet_grid(metric ~ W, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = OKABE) +
  labs(x = "D (cM)", y = NULL, colour = NULL)
```

- **AFR: the prediction cannot be judged by counts.** AFR names no point: C1
  holds at `r AN$AFR$counts$c1_met` of `r AN$AFR$counts$points` points (all at D
  `r paste(g(unlist(AN$AFR$counts$c1_holds_at_d)), collapse = ", ")` cM) and C2
  at `r AN$AFR$counts$c2_met`. Both AFR's and EUR's nearest per-lead points sit
  at the grid's smallest D, so a calibrated D for AFR would be at or below where
  the grid stops. What is observed fits the prediction without proving it: at
  W `r w_lab(AN$AFR$at[["d0.1_w1mb"]]$w_bp)`, AFR's ρ falls from
  `r f(AN$AFR$at[["d0.1_w1mb"]]$rho)` at D `r g(AN$AFR$at[["d0.1_w1mb"]]$d_cm)` cM to
  `r f(AN$AFR$at$bp_w1mb$rho)` bp-only, where EUR's goes from
  `r f(AN$EUR$at[["d0.1_w1mb"]]$rho)` to `r f(AN$EUR$at$bp_w1mb$rho)`; at W
  `r w_lab(AN$AFR$at$bp_w10mb$w_bp)` AFR's falls from `r f(AN$AFR$at[["d0.1_w10mb"]]$rho)` to `r f(AN$AFR$at$bp_w10mb$rho)`. C3 holds at every W for AFR
  (`r paste(paste0("W ", w_lab(AN$AFR$counts$c3$w_bp), ": D ", vapply(AN$AFR$counts$c3$d_cm_that_hold, function(d) paste(g(d), collapse = ", "), ""), " cM"), collapse = "; ")`),
  but on counts that C2 rejects.
- **AMR: usable to rank, not to choose D.** C1 holds at
  `r AN$AMR$counts$c1_met` of `r AN$AMR$counts$points` points (ρ
  `r f(AN$AMR$counts$rho_min)`–`r f(AN$AMR$counts$rho_max)`), but C2 at `r AN$AMR$counts$c2_met` of `r AN$AMR$counts$points`. The AMR panel has `r n(AN$AMR$samples)` samples, and
  `r pct(AN$AMR$chance_panel[["share_r2_ge_0.01"]], 2)` of its unlinked pairs
  reach r² `r R2P` by chance, against `r pct(AN$EUR$chance_panel[["share_r2_ge_0.01"]], 2)`
  in EUR, so its clump counts are partly chance. Admixture's long-range LD shows
  in the disagreements: at AMR's nearest point,
  `r pct(AN$AMR$nearest$splits$beyond_1mb_share)` of spurious splits lie more
  than `r w_lab(AN$AMR$nearest$splits$near_band_bp)` from their clump's index
  variant and `r pct(AN$AMR$nearest$splits$r2_ge_strong_share)` have r² of at
  least `r g(AN$AMR$nearest$splits$strong_r2)`, where chance gives `r pct(AN$AMR$chance_panel$share_r2_ge_strong, 2)`. For EUR the same shares
  are `r pct(AN$EUR$nearest$splits$beyond_1mb_share)` and `r pct(AN$EUR$nearest$splits$r2_ge_strong_share)`. No cM distance inside W
  separates such pairs.
- **EAS names `r pt_lab(AN$EAS$counts$named$d_cm, AN$EAS$counts$named$w_bp)`,**
  where C1 and C2 hold, but C3 holds at `r w_list(AN$EAS$counts$c3_holds_at_w)`:
  the named point ties bp-only at W `r w_lab(NAMED_W)`
  `r if (AN$EAS$named_ties_bp_w10mb) "exactly, on every count metric" else "only approximately"`,
  and bp-only at W `r w_lab(NAMED_W)`
  `r if (AN$EAS$bp_w10mb_meets_c1_c2) "meets C1 and C2 itself" else "fails C1 or C2"` (ρ
  `r f(AN$EAS$at$bp_w10mb$rho)`, median ratio `r f(AN$EAS$at$bp_w10mb$median_ratio)`). The EAS verdict rests on
  `r n(AN$EAS$tier_rows)` tier rows from `r n(AN$EAS$swept)` Analyses, none
  with largest |z| above `r f(AN$EAS$swept_max_abs_z, 1)`, so treat it as
  indicative.

```{r chance}
ch <- do.call(rbind, lapply(an, function(a) {
  r <- AN[[a]]
  data.frame(ancestry = a, samples = n(r$samples),
             pool = paste0(n(r$chance_panel$pool_variants), " / ", n(r$chance_panel$variants_used)),
             l = pct(r$chance_panel[["share_r2_ge_0.001"]]), p = pct(r$chance_panel[["share_r2_ge_0.01"]], 2),
             s = pct(r$chance_panel$share_r2_ge_strong, 3),
             il = pct(r$chance_index_pairs[["share_r2_ge_0.001"]]), ip = pct(r$chance_index_pairs[["share_r2_ge_0.01"]], 2),
             ipairs = n(r$chance_index_pairs$pairs_evaluable))
}))
kable(ch, row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("panel", "samples", "pooled variants / used",
                    paste0("panel: r² ≥ ", R2L), paste0("panel: r² ≥ ", R2P),
                    paste0("panel: r² ≥ ", g(AN$AMR$nearest$splits$strong_r2)),
                    paste0("index pairs: r² ≥ ", R2L), paste0("index pairs: r² ≥ ", R2P), "index pairs"),
      caption = paste0("Chance LD, two ways. The panel's own: ", n(AN$EUR$chance_panel$pairs), " seeded cross-chromosome pairs of the shared-set variants the swept Analyses hold, a property of the panel's sample size. Index pairs: cross-chromosome pairs of each swept Analysis's own index variants, which depend on how many hits the Analyses have (EAS has few)."))
```

### #406: what pruning costs {#cost}

**Question.** Is genetic-distance pruning actually cheaper than clumping, the
reason for considering it, and is it fast enough to run per query?

**Criteria.** Every number in the run's output with the machine, date and
commit; pruning against clumping as a ratio for the same Analyses; and whether
query-time pruning of the largest slice is fast enough per query. The budget,
fixed before measuring, was: `r CO$parameters$budget`. **Met**; the answer to
the last is no.

The run was on `r CO$measured_on`, on `r CO$machine$cpu_model`
(`r CO$machine$cores` cores), at engine commit `` `r CO$commit` ``, with
`r CO$parameters$repeats` repeats of each stage, the rule at
`r pt_lab(CO$parameters$d_cm, CO$parameters$w_bp)`, and plink2 on
`r CO$parameters$threads` threads.

**Building the cM array.** For `r PV$store`'s `r n(PV$variants)` variants,
reading chromosome and position from the Store Variant Table took
`r sec(PV$read_s, 1)` and interpolating cM `r sec(PV$interpolate_s, 1)`. The
per-variant chromosome, position and cM arrays together take
`r n(round(PV$mapped_bytes / 1e6))` MB, the cM array alone
`r n(round(PV$cm_bytes / 1e6))` MB, and `r n(PV$off_map)` variants on
`r paste(PV$off_map_chromosomes, collapse = ", ")` have no cM.

#406 timed two workloads, and each table below holds one. **Per query** is the
whole tier a Top-Hit Query returns, imputed rows included: this is what a
per-query option would prune. **Against clumping** is the shared set of the same
Analysis, the rows both methods can see: this is where pruning and clumping do
the same job. Each ratio follows from the two times beside it.

```{r cost}
sl <- CO$slices
slice_lab <- paste0(sl$store, " ", sl$analysis_id, " at ", vapply(sl$threshold, sci, ""))
kable(data.frame(slice = slice_lab, rows = n(sl$tier), query = sec(sl$query_s), resolved = sec(sl$resolved_query_s),
                 written = sec(sl$pruning_s), written_x = times(sl$ratio),
                 fast = sec(sl$fast_pruning_s), fast_x = times(sl$fast_ratio, 2),
                 of_resolved = f(sl$fast_ratio_of_resolved, 3)),
      row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("slice", "tier rows", "Top-Hit Query", "same query, resolved", "pruning as written",
                    "÷ query", "block rule with per-variant arrays", "÷ query", "÷ resolved query"),
      caption = "Per query, on the whole tier: what pruning adds to the query it follows. Medians of the repeats. Pruning as written reads positions from the Store Variant Table; the block-at-a-time rule gives the same leads and reads per-variant position and cM arrays.")
kable(data.frame(slice = slice_lab, rows = n(sl$shared_rows),
                 written = sec(sl$shared_pruning_s), fast = sec(sl$shared_fast_pruning_s),
                 plink2 = sec(sl$plink2_s), e2e = sec(sl$clumping_end_to_end_s),
                 r1 = f(sl$ratio_plink2, 3), r2 = f(sl$ratio_fast_plink2, 3), r3 = f(sl$ratio_fast_end_to_end, 3)),
      row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("slice", "shared-set rows", "pruning as written", "block rule", "plink2 alone",
                    "clumping, end to end", "as written ÷ plink2", "block rule ÷ plink2", "block rule ÷ end to end"),
      caption = "Against clumping, on the shared set of the same Analysis: pruning (the cM lookup and the rule) and clumping on the same rows. Clumping end to end includes matching the rows to the panel.")
```

```{r cost-pick}
# #406 fixed its budget on the 5e-8 tier of the largest Analysis; its 5e-4 tier is the largest slice by rows.
big <- sl[sl$analysis_id == sl$analysis_id[sl$name == CO$largest_by_rows] & sl$threshold == GRID$tier, ]
big4 <- sl[sl$name == CO$largest_by_rows, ]
big_lab <- paste0(big$analysis_id, "'s ", sci(big$threshold), " tier")
big4_lab <- paste0("its ", sci(big4$threshold), " tier")
art <- CO$artefact_analyses
```

- **Against clumping, on the shared set, pruning is cheaper on every slice.**
  Divided by plink2 alone, the rule as written costs
  `r f(CO$ratio_ranges$as_written_plink2_only$min, 3)`–`r f(CO$ratio_ranges$as_written_plink2_only$max, 3)`
  of clumping's time (`r times(CO$ratio_ranges$as_written_plink2_only$cheaper_min)`–`r times(CO$ratio_ranges$as_written_plink2_only$cheaper_max, 0)`
  cheaper), and the block rule
  `r f(CO$ratio_ranges$fast_plink2_only$min, 3)`–`r f(CO$ratio_ranges$fast_plink2_only$max, 3)`.
  Against clumping end to end, which must first match rows to the panel, the
  block rule is `r times(CO$ratio_ranges$fast_end_to_end$cheaper_min, 0)`–`r times(CO$ratio_ranges$fast_end_to_end$cheaper_max, 0)`
  cheaper.
- **Per query, on the whole tier, it misses the budget on `r nrow(sl) - CO$slices_within_budget` of `r nrow(sl)` slices.**
  #406 reported its budget on `r big_lab` (`r n(big$tier)` rows), where the
  Top-Hit Query takes `r sec(big$query_s)`. Pruning as written takes
  `r sec(big$pruning_s)` (`r times(big$ratio)` the query), of which reading
  positions from the Store Variant Table takes `r sec(big$positions_s, 1)`,
  against `r sec(big$positions_array_s, 3)` from a per-variant array. The block rule
  with per-variant arrays takes `r sec(big$fast_pruning_s)`
  (`r times(big$fast_ratio, 2)` the bare query, but
  `r f(big$fast_ratio_of_resolved, 3)` of the resolved query a reader actually
  waits for, `r sec(big$resolved_query_s, 1)`). The resolved query's own peak
  memory was `r n(round(big$resolved_query_peak_mb))` MB, from
  `r n(round(big$resolved_query_start_mb))` MB already resident. The largest
  slice by rows is `r big4_lab` (`r n(big4$tier)` rows): query
  `r sec(big4$query_s)`, pruning as written `r sec(big4$pruning_s)`
  (`r times(big4$ratio)`), block rule `r sec(big4$fast_pruning_s)`
  (`r times(big4$fast_ratio, 2)` the query, `r f(big4$fast_ratio_of_resolved, 3)`
  of the resolved query).
- `r if (CO$every_fast_rule_identical) "On every slice, the block rule gives the same leads as the rule as written." else "The block rule did not give the same leads on every slice."`
- **`r Word(nrow(art))` of the timed Analyses are artefact-like:** the ones #403's draw
  excludes by its row cap. At `r TIER`,
  `r paste0(art$analysis_id, " has ", n(art$rows_abs_z_over), " of its ", n(art$tier), " tier rows past |z| ", art$over_abs_z, collapse = ", and ")`.
  They are timed for cost only.

Absolute seconds carry the node's load: its load average reached
`r f(CO$max_load, 1)` during the run. The ratios and the share of each stage
are what to compare.

### #409: boundaries from the data

**Question.** #403 showed that per-lead disagreement concentrates at strong
peaks. Would locus boundaries taken from the data do better than a fixed
distance? Two rules were tried on #403's Analyses, shared set and clumps:

- **peak prominence:** two `r TIER` hits stay in one locus unless the |z|
  profile between them, read from the `r sci(PR$profile_tier)` tier as the
  maximum |z| per bin of B bp, falls into a valley. A row joins the strongest
  accepted lead whose lowest bin between them stays above a threshold (relative,
  f × the row's |z|, or a fixed chain of non-empty bins), and no merge spans
  more than the clumping window. B ∈ {`r paste(g(PR$bins_bp / 1e3), collapse = ", ")`} kb;
  thresholds `r paste(PR$thresholds, collapse = ", ")`.
- **one lead per LD block:** the strongest row in each of the
  `r n(PR$blocks)` EUR LD blocks of the panel's region file.

**Criteria.** C1 and C2 in #403's wording (C2 restricts the profile to HapMap3
as well as the hits); C3's margins against bp-only at W `r w_lab(NAMED_W)` and
at each other W; per-lead rates by the lead's |z| band; every valley that
separates two leads classed as low |z| or no tier row, with a sample checked
against the Store. **Met.** At #403's named point, W `r w_lab(NAMED_W)`,
`r if (length(C3_AT_NAMED) == 0) "neither rule beats distance pruning: C3 holds there for no rule" else paste("C3 holds there for", paste(C3_AT_NAMED, collapse = "; "))`.
Elsewhere on the grid, `r C3_ELSEWHERE`.

```{r profile}
rl <- PR$rules
bl <- PR$baselines
prof <- rbind(
  data.frame(rule = rl$label, rho = f(rl$rho), c1 = yes(rl$c1), ratio = f(rl$median_ratio), log2 = f(rl$median_abs_log2),
             c2 = yes(rl$c2), d = paste0(sprintf("%+.3f", rl$delta_rho_w10mb), " / ", sprintf("%+.3f", rl$delta_abs_log2_w10mb)),
             c3 = vapply(rl$c3_holds_at_w, w_list, ""),
             rates = paste0(pct(rl$spurious_split_rate), " / ", pct(rl$lost_signal_rate)),
             strong = pct(rl$strong_disagreement), named = rl$named_analysis_leads),
  data.frame(rule = paste0("#403 ", pt_lab(bl$d_cm, bl$w_bp)), rho = f(bl$rho), c1 = yes(bl$c1), ratio = f(bl$median_ratio),
             log2 = f(bl$median_abs_log2), c2 = yes(bl$c2), d = "", c3 = "",
             rates = paste0(pct(bl$spurious_split_rate), " / ", pct(bl$lost_signal_rate)),
             strong = pct(bl$strong_disagreement), named = bl$named_analysis_leads))
kable(prof, row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("rule", "ρ", "C1", "median density ratio", "median |log2|", "C2",
                    paste0("Δρ / Δ|log2| against bp-only, W ", w_lab(NAMED_W)), "C3 holds at",
                    "spurious / lost", paste0("disagreement, leads with |z| ≥ ", g(rl$strong_from[1])),
                    paste0("Locus Leads in ", PR$named_analysis$analysis_id, " (", PR$named_analysis$index_variants, " clumps)")),
      caption = paste0("The prominence and LD-block rules on #403's ", PR$analyses, " Analyses at r² ", R2P, ", beside #403's named point and the tracer's point. Δ|log2| is positive when the rule is less density-sensitive than bp-only."))
```

- **C3 holds at W `r w_lab(NAMED_W)` for `r if (length(C3_AT_NAMED) == 0) "no rule" else paste(C3_AT_NAMED, collapse = "; ")`.**
  At any W it holds for `r if (length(C3_ALL) == 0) "no rule" else paste(C3_ALL, collapse = "; ")`.
- **Narrow bins fail C2.** `r PR$narrow_bin_c2_met` of the
  `r PR$narrow_bin_rules` B `r g(min(PR$bins_bp) / 1e3)` kb rules meet it
  (median ratio `r f(PR$narrow_bin_ratio_min, 2)`–`r f(PR$narrow_bin_ratio_max, 2)`):
  on HapMap3 the profile has gaps that read as valleys, so the rule finds more
  loci on the sparse axis, not fewer.
- **LD blocks** rank well (ρ `r f(rl$rho[rl$rule == "ld_blocks"])`) but are
  more density-sensitive than bp-only (median |log2|
  `r f(rl$median_abs_log2[rl$rule == "ld_blocks"])` against `r f(bl$median_abs_log2[is.na(bl$d_cm)])`). Rows outside every block are
  counted: `r PR$blocks_rows_outside` rows in `r PR$blocks_stretches_outside`
  stretches.
- **At strong peaks** (leads with |z| ≥ `r g(rl$strong_from[1])`),
  `r paste(rl$label[rl$beats_named_at_strong_peaks], collapse = "; ")` disagree
  with clumping clearly less often than bp-only at W `r w_lab(NAMED_W)`.
  Against `r TP`, `r if (any(rl$beats_tracer_at_strong_peaks)) paste(paste(rl$label[rl$beats_tracer_at_strong_peaks], collapse = "; "), "do") else "no rule does"`.
- **Valleys are real, not gaps.** There are `r n(PR$valleys$no_row_valleys)`
  distinct valleys with no tier row. In a sample of
  `r PR$valleys$by_bin$sampled[1]` per bin width checked against the Store,
  `r paste(paste0(pct(PR$valleys$by_bin$share_gap), " (B ", g(PR$valleys$by_bin$bin_bp / 1e3), " kb)"), collapse = " and ")`
  are gaps in coverage rather than low |z|, so the stop rule, which withholds
  the judgement when gaps dominate a sample, `r if (any(PR$valleys$by_bin$stop_rule_trips)) "tripped" else "did not trip"`.

## What it means for `n_loci_*`

The owner has decided the following; #407's verdict on #62 will record it.

- **`n_loci_*` uses the bp-only window at W `r w_lab(NAMED_W)` for EUR and
   EAS,** with no cM limit and no per-variant cM array.
   - EUR: it is #403's named point. C1 holds (ρ `r f(AN$EUR$at$bp_w10mb$rho)`),
     C2 holds (median density ratio `r f(AN$EUR$at$bp_w10mb$median_ratio)`,
     median |log2| `r f(AN$EUR$at$bp_w10mb$median_abs_log2)` against a limit of `r f(EC$rows$c2_abs_log2_limit)`), and it loses the fewest leads to density
     (`r pct(AN$EUR$at$bp_w10mb$lost_to_density)`). C3 holds at
     `r w_list(EC$c3_holds_at_w)``r if (MP$c3_nowhere) ", on any of the maps #404 compared" else ""`.
   - EAS: bp-only at W `r w_lab(NAMED_W)`
     `r if (AN$EAS$bp_w10mb_meets_c1_c2) "meets C1 and C2" else "fails C1 or C2"` (ρ
     `r f(AN$EAS$at$bp_w10mb$rho)`, median ratio `r f(AN$EAS$at$bp_w10mb$median_ratio)`)`r if (AN$EAS$named_ties_bp_w10mb) " and ties the named cM point" else ""`;
     C3 holds at `r w_list(AN$EAS$counts$c3_holds_at_w)`.
   - So in both, cM adds nothing the counts can see.
- **AFR and AMR get no `n_loci_*` until they are calibrated.** No grid point
   meets both C1 and C2 there (`r AN$AFR$counts$both_met` of
   `r AN$AFR$counts$points` in AFR, `r AN$AMR$counts$both_met` in AMR).
   - AFR: C2 holds nowhere, and C1 only at D
     `r paste(g(unlist(AN$AFR$counts$c1_holds_at_d)), collapse = ", ")` cM. At W
     `r w_lab(AN$AFR$at$bp_w10mb$w_bp)`, bp-only's ρ is
     `r f(AN$AFR$at$bp_w10mb$rho)` against `r f(AN$AFR$at[["d0.1_w10mb"]]$rho)` at
     D `r g(AN$AFR$at[["d0.1_w10mb"]]$d_cm)` cM, so the rule the other ancestries
     use ranks AFR Analyses poorly.
   - AMR: C1 holds everywhere, C2 nowhere, and the AMR panel's chance LD at r²
     `r R2P` (`r pct(AN$AMR$chance_panel[["share_r2_ge_0.01"]], 2)`) leaves its
     clumps too noisy to calibrate against.
- **No follow-up tickets are planned.**

The alternatives, with their numbers on the same EUR Analyses:

```{r alternatives}
blk <- rl[rl$rule == "ld_blocks", ]
p75 <- rl[rl$label == PR$c3_anywhere$label[1], ]
bcm <- pick(EC$configs, EC$named_cm$d_cm, EC$named_cm$w_bp)
tpc <- pick(EC$configs, TP_D, TP_W)
tpl <- pick(EPL$points, TP_D, TP_W)
bpc <- pick(EC$configs, NA, NAMED_W)
bpl <- pick(EPL$points, NA, NAMED_W)
alt <- data.frame(
  option = c(paste0("chosen: ", NAMED), paste0("best cM point: ", pt_lab(EC$named_cm$d_cm, EC$named_cm$w_bp)),
             paste0("tracer's cM point: ", TP), "one lead per LD block", paste0("prominence, ", p75$label)),
  rho = f(c(bpc$rho, bcm$rho, tpc$rho, blk$rho, p75$rho)),
  log2 = f(c(bpc$median_abs_log2, bcm$median_abs_log2, tpc$median_abs_log2, blk$median_abs_log2, p75$median_abs_log2)),
  lost = pct(c(bpc$lost_to_density, bcm$lost_to_density, tpc$lost_to_density, blk$lost_to_density, p75$lost_to_density)),
  c3 = c("(the baseline)", w_list(EC$c3_holds_at_w), w_list(EC$c3_holds_at_w),
         w_list(blk$c3_holds_at_w), w_list(p75$c3_holds_at_w)),
  rates = paste0(pct(c(bpl$spurious_split_rate, NA, tpl$spurious_split_rate, blk$spurious_split_rate, p75$spurious_split_rate)),
                 " / ", pct(c(bpl$lost_signal_rate, NA, tpl$lost_signal_rate, blk$lost_signal_rate, p75$lost_signal_rate))),
  needs = c("positions only", "a per-variant cM array", "a per-variant cM array", "an LD-block file per ancestry",
            paste("the", sci(PR$profile_tier), "tier as a profile")))
alt$rates[2] <- paste0(pct(pick(EPL$points, EC$named_cm$d_cm, EC$named_cm$w_bp)$spurious_split_rate), " / ",
                       pct(pick(EPL$points, EC$named_cm$d_cm, EC$named_cm$w_bp)$lost_signal_rate))
kable(alt, row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("rule", "ρ (C1)", "median |log2| (C2)", "leads lost to density", "C3 holds at",
                    paste0("spurious / lost at r² ", R2P), "what it needs"),
      caption = "The chosen rule beside the alternatives the prototype measured, on #403's EUR Analyses.")
```

### Still open: build time only, or per query as well?

One question is left for the owner after reading this report: whether pruning
runs only at build time, giving `n_loci_*` as Analytical Metadata in
`analyses.tsv`, or also as a per-query option of the Top-Hit Query. #406's
numbers bear on both. It timed the rule at
`r pt_lab(CO$parameters$d_cm, CO$parameters$w_bp)`; the chosen bp-only window
was not timed. The cM lookup the chosen rule drops took
`r sec(big$cm_s, 3)` on `r big_lab`. The figures below are for that tier
(`r n(big$tier)` rows), with `r big4_lab`, the largest slice by rows
(`r n(big4$tier)`), in brackets.

- **Build time.** A Store pays once per Analysis and tier: here
  `r sec(big$positions_s, 1)` (`r sec(big4$positions_s, 1)`) to read positions
  from the Store Variant Table and `r sec(big$rule_s, 1)`
  (`r sec(big4$rule_s, 1)`) for the rule as written, or
  `r sec(big$rule_fast_s, 1)` (`r sec(big4$rule_fast_s, 1)`) for the block rule. The bp-only rule
  needs no cM array, so `r PV$store` would not carry its
  `r n(round(PV$cm_bytes / 1e6))` MB of cM nor pay the
  `r sec(PV$interpolate_s, 1)` to interpolate it.
- **Per query.** The Top-Hit Query takes `r sec(big$query_s)`
  (`r sec(big4$query_s)`) and the resolved query
  `r sec(big$resolved_query_s, 1)` (`r sec(big4$resolved_query_s, 1)`). Pruning
  as written adds `r sec(big$pruning_s, 1)` (`r sec(big4$pruning_s, 1)`):
  `r times(big$ratio)` (`r times(big4$ratio)`) the query,
  `r f(big$pruning_over_resolved, 2)` (`r f(big4$pruning_over_resolved, 2)`) of
  the resolved query. The block rule with per-variant chromosome and position
  arrays, which Stores do not carry today
  (`r n(round(PV$position_bytes / 1e6))` MB for `r PV$store`), adds
  `r sec(big$fast_pruning_s)` (`r sec(big4$fast_pruning_s)`):
  `r times(big$fast_ratio, 2)` (`r times(big4$fast_ratio, 2)`) the query,
  `r f(big$fast_ratio_of_resolved, 3)` (`r f(big4$fast_ratio_of_resolved, 3)`)
  of the resolved query. By the budget
  fixed before measuring, `r if (CO$slices_within_budget == 0) "no slice qualifies" else paste(CO$slices_within_budget, "slices qualify")`
  for per-query pruning.

## Limitations

- **Small panels and chance LD.** The reference is clumping on panels of
  `r n(AN$EUR$samples)` (EUR) down to `r n(AN$AMR$samples)` (AMR) samples. At
  these sizes `r pct(AN$EUR$chance_panel[["share_r2_ge_0.001"]], 0)` of
  unlinked EUR pairs reach r² `r R2L` and
  `r pct(AN$AMR$chance_panel[["share_r2_ge_0.01"]], 1)` of unlinked AMR pairs
  reach r² `r R2P`. Clump counts are themselves noisy at low r², which is why
  the counts are judged at r² `r R2P` and AMR is not calibrated.
- **EAS is thin.** `r n(AN$EAS$swept)` Analyses and `r n(AN$EAS$tier_rows)`
  tier rows, from a pool of `r n(AN$EAS$pool)` in which
  `r n(AN$EAS$no_observed_rows)` have no Observed Association at `r TIER`, and
  `r AN$EAS$z_quota_in_pool` have a largest |z| of
  `r EUR$selection$quota_z_from` or more. Its C2 verdict may not survive a
  larger draw.
- **AFR's panel fit.** `r AN$AFR$below_floor` of `r AN$AFR$drawn` drawn AFR
  Analyses fell under the shared-set floor:
  `r AN$AFR$below_floor_groups$near_floor` keep
  `r pct(AN$AFR$below_floor_groups$near_floor_min)`–`r pct(AN$AFR$below_floor_groups$near_floor_max)`
  of their rows, and `r AN$AFR$below_floor_groups$far` keep at most `r pct(AN$AFR$below_floor_groups$far_max)`. The missing rows are rare variants
  below the AFR panel's minor-allele-count filter, so the panel, not the
  matching, limits AFR.
- **Artefact Analyses excluded.**
  `r paste(EUR$selection$excluded_over_max_rows$analysis_id, collapse = " and ")`
  exceed #403's row cap of `r n(EUR$selection$max_observed_rows)` observed rows,
  and
  `r paste(pct(over_share(EUR$selection$excluded_over_max_rows$analysis_id), 0), collapse = " and ")`
  of their tier rows, respectively, lie past |z| `r big$over_abs_z`. They are left out of every
  sweep and timed only for cost.
- **Load on the timing node.** #406's absolute times carry a load average of up
  to `r f(CO$max_load, 1)`; compare its ratios, not its seconds.
- **The draw is the committed one.** The EUR selection was drawn on the Store
  inventory of `r EUR$selection$committed_on`. Drawing again today lists
  OGS-00024, OGS-00025 and OGS-00026 among the Stores left out (signals-only or
  cis coverage); the pool and the chosen Analyses are unchanged.
- **Untested.** A pedigree map (deCODE) and D below `r g(min(GRID$d_cm))` cM for
  AFR were not run, and #406 did not time the chosen bp-only rule itself.

## Reproduce {#reproduce}

This page reads one file, `docs/data/locus-leads-prototype.json`, written by
`tools/locus_leads_prototype_extract.py` from the engine's committed outputs at
`` `r x$engine$commit` `` (opengwas/opengwasdb, branch `orch/62-locus-leads`).
The extract reads each output with `git show` and records its sha256. Where a
later ticket's output copies #403's numbers (#404's record of the pyrho mean,
#409's baselines, rows, criteria and per-Analysis records), every field the copy
shares with #403's output must be equal, at any depth; so must #405's grid and
criteria, each sweep's selection digest, the panel sizes, and each ratio #406
publishes against the two times it divides. Otherwise the extract refuses,
naming the field and both values, and writes nothing.
`tests/locus-leads-extract/` tests these refusals on synthetic outputs. A
re-run at the same commit reproduces the extract byte for byte.

```{bash}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
pixi run -e dev python3 tools/locus_leads_prototype_extract.py \
    --engine <an opengwasdb checkout holding the commit> --commit 06d1a43 \
    --output docs/data/locus-leads-prototype.json
quarto render docs/reports/locus-leads-prototype.qmd --to html
```

The engine's own commands for each output are in
`prototypes/locus_leads/README.md` and in each per-ticket report under
`docs/benchmark-output/locus_leads/`.

```{r sources}
src <- x$sources
kable(data.frame(path = paste0("`", sub("^docs/benchmark-output/locus_leads/", "", src$path), "`"),
                 ticket = src$ticket, bytes = n(src$bytes), sha256 = paste0("`", src$sha256, "`")),
      row.names = FALSE, col.names = c("output", "ticket", "bytes", "sha256"),
      caption = paste0("The engine outputs this page reads, under docs/benchmark-output/locus_leads/ at ", substr(x$engine$commit, 1, 7), "."))
```
